key_insight: DEFEAT enables gradient-based crystal design across composition and structure, including semiconductor candidates targeting a 1.34 eV band gap for photovoltaic absorption.
engineering_relevance: Jointly optimizing elements, atom counts, positions, and lattice vectors could accelerate the search for solar absorber materials with suitable band gaps and competitive stability.
method: Extend a pretrained EquiformerV3 model to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Combine gradients from fine-tuned property models with a learned energy penalty.
Validate candidate band gaps and stability using SCAN calculations and assess finite-temperature competition with machine-learned potentials.
evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirmed ten novel crystal structures with band gaps within 20% of 1.34 eV on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias can propagate into designs unless corrected in the objective; these computational candidates are not demonstrated solar cells.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
